## Example 1.2(d–f) {#dc1-example-1-2-def .dc-lesson}

<p>Differentiate the following expressions with respect to <span data-math="x"></span>.</p>
<div class="dc-problem-list"><div><span class="part">d)</span><span data-math="y=e^{-x}"></span></div><div><span class="part">e)</span><span data-math="y=-2e^{1-4x}"></span></div><div><span class="part">f)</span><span data-math="y=e^{\frac{x}{2}}"></span></div></div><p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 2 · Example 1.2(d–f)</p>

::: notes
(d) y'=-e^(-x). (e) y'=8e^(1-4x). (f) y'=1/2 e^(x/2). Ask students to identify the derivative of each exponent before calculating. In (e), the two negative factors give a positive derivative; the original function has negative values but is increasing. Do not conflate sign of function and sign of derivative. About five minutes for both Example 1.2 slides together.
:::
